free_tier.stated: Each record comes with a default quota of 50 GB and an unlimited number of records may be uploaded under 50 GB; a further 150 GB additional allowance is held per account and can be distributed across records as needed.
free_tier.notes: CERN funds the service, so the quota is a policy that can move; it is not a purchased allowance with a contract behind it.

per_object_cap.notes: A record is the upload unit, not a file: up to 100 files may sit in one record, and their total volume may not exceed 50 GB.

retention.stated: Items are retained for the lifetime of the repository, currently the lifetime of the host laboratory CERN, whose experimental programme is defined for the next 20 years at least; a withdrawn record leaves a tombstone page and the DOI and URL of the original object are retained.
retention.notes: Permanence is the whole point of a DOI, and it is also why this is an archive rather than a working set.

egress.terms: free with no metered allowance; the published limits are on request count, not on transferred bytes: a guest may make 60 requests per minute, an authenticated user 100; files are served to an anonymous ranged GET without authentication.

interface_detail: REST deposit API with a token, plus an S3-compatible endpoint for large files. Not a WebDAV or rclone-native backend.
tooling: requests or curl against the deposit API; the S3 endpoint needs a generated key pair
chaining: The useful chain is write-once archive plus a parallel ranged reader: Zenodo holds the durable copy and a Worker or a ranged client serves it, because a single stream is slow but many streams are not.

limits.value: 50 GB per record, and 150 GB total per account
a DOI is minted on publish and the record is then immutable except for metadata; files may only be added in a 30-day window

limits_note: A second record is the alternative route and it costs a second DOI.
binding_note: The cap is generous for a user's shard sizes; the gate is what decides the workflow, because a mistake after publication cannot be corrected in place, only superseded by a new version.

identity_cost.detail: A local account asks for a username, full name, affiliation, email address and password, and the email must be confirmed before the first upload; ORCID and GitHub logins are offered as alternatives and neither is required. No card and no institutional check.

reliability_note: CERN-operated and long-lived; the failure mode is policy change rather than downtime. Records are immutable after publication, so a quota reduction would affect new deposits and not existing ones. The binding limit on reading is the per-connection throttle, which parallel ranged GETs defeat; see zenodo-anonymous-download-throughput.
confidence_note: The quota and the write gate are read from CERN's own help pages on 2026-10-21; the throughput is measured separately in zenodo-anonymous-download-throughput.

evidence.proved: 50 GB per record and a 150 GB per-account pool, stated as a shared allowance rather than a per-record guarantee
the retention policy: records are retained permanently and citable by DOI
the 50 GB per-record default and the unlimited record count; the same page states the additional 150 GB allowance is distributed from a per-account pool
